fixtures.source: The incident record concerns the preview service rather than the main application. Between 10:05 and 10:12 UTC, preview requests returned HTTP 503. The main application continued serving requests during that interval. Investigation found that the preview process could not acquire its local lock. The log contained the exact message "preview lock unavailable". We have not established who held that lock, so the handoff must not name an owner as though that were known. Restarting the preview process restored previews at 10:12 UTC. That is the observed recovery, not evidence that the lock ownership question has been solved. The supporting log is incident-preview-8. The next step belongs to Oren, who will add lock-owner diagnostics and reproduce the contention in a disposable fixture. The purpose of this handoff is to allow someone who did not see the incident discussion to understand the affected surface, the recovery and the remaining investigation.

fixtures.task: Write a concise standalone API migration note.
fixtures.source: This note should explain the change to the pagination response and should preserve the compatibility details rather than merely saying that pagination was improved. Version 2 adds the next_cursor field. Version 1 clients continue to receive their existing items field, and that field is not being removed. A null next_cursor means that the captured result has no further page. Results are captured once for a query. Files created after that capture do not appear in later pages of the same result. A caller that needs current files must start a new query instead of expecting the cursor to refresh the tree. Cursor state expires when the run is retired. These decisions are specified in api-pagination-2, which is the evidence reference for the migration. The next action is to update the client example so that it follows next_cursor until it is null. There is no change to write permissions or file ownership as part of this API change.

Version 1 items remains available.

fixtures.task: Write a standalone retention decision.
fixtures.source: The retention decision applies to generated preview artifacts. It does not apply to the original source documents, and that distinction should not be lost in shortening the note. Preview artifacts become eligible for cleanup after seven days without access. Eligibility is not the same as deletion: the first operation produces a preview of the candidates and does not delete them. A pinned artifact is excluded even if it is older than seven days. Applying cleanup requires the exact candidate revision from the preview; if an artifact changes before apply, that artifact is skipped and reported as changed. There is no automatic replay of skipped deletions. The decision is captured in retention-review-2. The next step is to test a pinned artifact and an artifact changed between preview and apply. No assertion has yet been made that those tests have passed, so the note must keep them as next actions.
